title: Japan, Okinawa, Iceland and the Caribbean
summary: The tour was redirected to Japan; Moore describes an engine failure flight, Christmas on a base, then Iceland and the Virgin Islands.

blocks.x: So you essentially went around the world with Louie Armstrong.

I was going to finish that, we were going to go back to New York by way of Paris and London and New York and within the space of five hours, Frenchie, the road manager, said, plans had been changed, we were going to Japan, so we went to Japan, and stayed there a month and in between Tokyo we went to Okinawa and we played in Okinawa for the service people and it was one of the roughest times on the plane during that storm when we had to get back into Tokyo.
What time of the year was this, was it summer?

I think it was spring. And I saw the hotel where we were staying was the beach where the Japs landed during the war and we had to get to Tokyo for an engagement and come rain, shine, wind and mostly wind. We went to the airport, we got in a plane and we left the airport and in about 10, 15 minutes in the air, there was an announcement in Japanese, it was a Japanese flight, there was an announcement that something was happening -- I don't know, I can't speak Japanese but the woman next to me, Japanese, she flew up in the air -- I said, "What's

the matter? What's the matter? What's the matter? She said, 'One engine stop, we go back.' So we went back again. Then we had to wait for another plane and fortunately the wind died down a little bit. That part Okinawa, in that of the world the wind hits there---nothing to stop it; that ocean is just flat, you know. When there's wind, you feel that wind. So we got another plane and this time we made it. So we went back to Tokyo and played Sendai, Hiroshima, Honshu. We played the naval base, at the naval base it was Christmas Day and one of the boys was doing his solo out front, the band was sitting in the back of the bandstand. I talked to Louie and I said, 'Please, Louie, could we go home. This is the first time I'm away from home on Christmas.' He said, 'Yes, Chief, I'm tired, I want to go home myself. We'll go home. Wait until we get back to San Francisco, we're going to go home. From Tokyo, we left Tokyo... we landed in San Francisco and we played a week in San Francisco and then from San Francisco we came back to New York.
